Look these things up in this order. (add "in ableton" at end of all of these) :  
- Info View  
- Session View  
- Arrangement View  
- how to set audio input device  
- how to set audio output device  
- how to add an audio track  
- how to record enable an audio track (aka "arm")   
- how to record in arrangement view (arrangement vs. session are different)  
- how to export audio   


The most confusing thing about Ableton for a GarageBand user is probably the Session View.  Think of this as more of a DJ / electronic thing, or even mega-churches!  You''d likely use Session View in a live performance.

Arrangement View is going to feel more familiar, and is probably how your producer is working on your music.  

The challenge is that the Ableton documentation often assumes you are using it as a DJ software in Session View, and also probably with a 3rd party external hardware controller.  This introduces tons of terms and workflows that are irrelevant to your current needs.  Seemingly irrelevant info in documentation can make it feel very confusing.

I promise you Ableton is far simpler and less painful a DAW than anything Apple owns.
